description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Regression introduced by ancora-rdx, already merged to main.

Concrete failure: mix test fails roughly 1 run in 3 with ExUnit.TimeoutError after 60000ms. Measured on main plus the ancora-p47 branch: run 1 green, run 2 = 2 failures (Ancora.Scaffold.FreshAdopterTest "fresh adopter goes from unanchored red to tagged green" and Mix.Tasks.Spec.PrimeTest "prime routes usage and environment failures without a verdict", both ExUnit.TimeoutError), run 3 green. The implementer on ancora-p47 hit the same thing independently.

Cause: test/support/ancora_case.exs:133 seed_build_path!/1 does File.cp_r!(Mix.Project.build_path(), build_path) on EVERY run_mix_subprocess call, and there are about 30 such calls per full run. That is roughly 135 MB of copying per suite. It was introduced by ancora-rdx to give each subprocess its own MIX_BUILD_PATH, which was correct in intent — the previous shared build path was a source of lock contention — but the per-call copy is expensive enough that under load a single subprocess test exceeds the 60 second ExUnit timeout.

Both graders saw the cost and rated it affordable. The cold verifier note read: "seed_build_path! does a File.cp_r! of _build/test (4.5 MB) on every subprocess call ... The suite still finishes in 32 seconds, so it is affordable now, but it is why the touched-file run alone takes 25 seconds and it will scale with _build." That judgement was wrong at the 1-in-3 rate now observed, and it is worth recording as a lesson: a cost flagged as affordable should be measured under repetition, not at one sample.

Fix direction (implementer choice, but do not simply raise the timeout — that hides it): seed ONE build path per suite or per test module and reuse it across subprocess calls, rather than copying per call. A hardlink or clone copy is another option on APFS. Whatever shape you choose, each subprocess must still not share a mutable build directory with a CONCURRENT one, which is the property ancora-rdx was buying.

Verification: full suite run 10 times consecutively with zero failures and no ExUnit.TimeoutError, on both CI matrix legs (Elixir 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1 and 1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5). Report the wall-clock of each run so the improvement is visible. Do not weaken any assertion and do not raise the ExUnit timeout to pass.

Status note (2026-09-03, orchestrator Phase 0): the co-landing sentence below is stale. ancora-8t2 was closed as superseded and its CI fix folded into ancora-xla.5. ancora-p47 is already implemented on its own stage branch and awaiting cold verification. This ticket no longer has to ride either of them; it is the epic's own prerequisite.

Measured again on the ancora-xla epic worktree at base 5d9cb40 with no code changes: 331 tests, 7 failures, wall clock 210s against the 32s baseline this ticket records. Every failure was ExUnit.TimeoutError inside run_mix_subprocess, three of them the exact tests named above. Host load average was 162 on 10 cores at the time, so contention amplified the defect rather than causing it: the same test passes alone, but takes 28 seconds by itself, which is the _build copy cost and nothing else.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: the full suite, run 10 times consecutively with zero failures and no ExUnit.TimeoutError, on both CI matrix legs (Elixir 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1 and 1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5). Report each run's wall clock so the improvement is visible. If host load is above roughly 2 per core, say so with the measured figure rather than reporting a number that load explains.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a subprocess mix run no longer copies the whole build path per call; (2) two concurrent subprocess tests still never share a mutable build directory, which is the isolation property ancora-rdx bought; (3) the single-test wall clock for test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs drops well below its current 28 seconds.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: the three named timeout-prone files plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier (implementer, capped at 2 runs as always): the compile-graph-scoped set plus mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission. Because the diff touches test/support/ancora_case.exs, which nearly every test file loads, that scoped set is effectively the whole suite; that is the correct scope here and does not need to be argued up to a separate full-suite run. Report the wall clock of the run. Do NOT attempt the ten-run repetition; it does not fit the capped cadence and is not your job.
  - Verifier tier: this is the one ticket whose verifier deliberately runs the full suite repeatedly. Ten consecutive full-suite runs with zero failures and no ExUnit.TimeoutError, each one's wall clock reported, plus mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission. Repetition is the whole proof, because the defect is a frequency rather than a single failure. Record the host load average alongside the runs so a slow number is attributable.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Do not raise the ExUnit timeout, do not weaken an assertion, and do not mark a test async: false to dodge the contention.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
- proves: the suite is green ten times running, and each subprocess test still gets its own build directory.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- test/support/ancora_case.exs (seed_build_path!/1 and run_mix_subprocess/2)
- test/support/**
- test/test_helper.exs
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth, or shrink for this ticket's own changes; never weakening a must)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/**
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (ancora-xla.5 owns it)
- mix.exs, VERSION, CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (intent):
- no raising the ExUnit timeout, globally or per test or per module
- no weakening or deleting an assertion to make a slow test pass
- no removing the per-subprocess build isolation that ancora-rdx introduced
- no production code changes; this is test infrastructure only

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test, ten consecutive green runs with wall clocks reported (orchestrator merge gate and verifier tier, not the implementer)
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

VERIFY: PASS (agent verify-p47s1o, opus, cold; relayed by the orchestrator — stacked verify of ancora-p47 + ancora-s1o)
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Commit 35372ed touches ONLY test/support/ancora_case.exs, inside this ticket's Allowed touches. No assertion weakened, no test deleted, no ExUnit timeout raised (stack-wide counts: base 374 test / 109 refute / 910 assert, head 376 / 110 / 913, the delta being exactly the two new ancora-p47 tests).

Safety argument — VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, and it holds for a stronger reason than the implementer gave:
- The sequencing claim is true and was confirmed against ExUnit 1.18.1 rather than assumed. ExUnit.Runner.run_tests/4 at runner.ex:382 is an Enum.reduce_while over the module's tests; each iteration calls run_test then spawn_test, and spawn_test blocks in receive_test_reply until the test replies or times out. Two tests of the same module cannot overlap. async: true parallelizes at the MODULE level only.
- The memo is not a table anywhere. setup_all computes the path once per module and returns it in the module context; the injected per-test setup copies it into the test process's dictionary; and the actual seed-once guard is `unless File.dir?(build_path)` — the FILESYSTEM is the memo. It is per-module because the path is per-module, so there is no shared state to race on.
- Module collision is not reachable: the path is _build/ancora-mix-#{TempName.cross_vm_suffix()} and cross_vm_suffix/0 is "#{System.pid()}_#{Base.encode16(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(6))}" — 48 bits per module across the 30 that use the template, with the OS pid separating concurrent VMs.
- The reuse is SAFER than this ticket's framing assumed: all 30 run_mix_subprocess call sites pass --root <fixture> as an argument and none passes a cd: option, so every subprocess runs mix from the ancora project root. The shared build path only ever receives ancora's own artifacts, identical on every call, so after the first seed each later call is a no-op recompile. Stale-fixture cross-contamination is not possible here.

Cleanup: the build path is removed by the on_exit registered inside setup_all, so it goes at module teardown rather than per call, AND that teardown runs on the failure path — run_setup_all/4 calls exec_on_exit(test_module, module_pid, timeout) at runner.ex:371 OUTSIDE the case, so it fires on the :ok branch, the setup_all :error branch, and the :DOWN crash branch alike; individual test failures do not skip it. Empirically _build/ancora-mix-* was 0 before the 10 runs and 0 after every one of them. The 24 modules that never call the helper pay only an rm_rf of a nonexistent path plus an on_exit registration and create no directory.

Clone fallback: clone_build_path!/2 shells out to /bin/cp -cR, and non-darwin platforms never reach it because seed_build_path!/1 branches on :os.type() and uses File.cp_r!/2 directly. On ANY non-zero cp exit (including a non-APFS volume where -c fails) it does File.rm_rf!(build_path) FIRST and then File.cp_r!/2, so a partial clone is wiped before the portable copy rather than left in place. Nothing is silent: if the portable copy also fails, cp_r! raises; if /bin/cp were absent, System.cmd raises :enoent.

Re-runs — the repetition IS the point of this ticket, so a single green run would prove nothing:
- full suite x10, sequential, nothing else running: 333 tests / 3 properties / 0 failures on every run, wall clocks 56s, 43s, 48s, 37s, 34s, 43s, 36s, 60s, 45s, 65s. Exit 0 on all ten, ZERO ExUnit.TimeoutError lines anywhere, zero _build/ancora-mix-* leftovers after each.
- Compare against the pre-fix measurements: the orchestrator saw 1 failure-run in 3, and the implementer's own repro run took 122s wall clock and timed out in FreshAdopterTest.
- spec.check --base 5d9cb40 -> result=pass. mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both exit 0.

Verdict: PASS. Gaps: none.

Notes (advisory, non-blocking): one narrow residual, PRE-EXISTING rather than introduced — on ExUnit.TimeoutError the runner does Process.exit(test_pid, :kill) at runner.ex:487 and moves on, so an orphaned mix child could in principle still be writing into the build path the next test reuses. The old code was arguably worse here, since it rm_rf'd the build path out from under any such orphan. It only matters after a test has already failed. Also: the `unless File.dir?` guard is what keeps cp -cR from producing a nested build_path/test directory — correct, but load-bearing; the File.rm_rf!(build_path) in setup_all backs it up.

Per agreement with the ancora-xla orchestrator, this ticket is NOT being closed here; it stays in_progress for that epic to close with the merge SHA as evidence.

title: Per-subprocess _build copy makes the suite time out about one run in three
